branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Progressive Multisystem Syndrome with Polyarticular Arthritis and Dermal Papules

state.case_summary:
A man in his 50s presented with pink-purple dermal papules and polyarticular inflammatory arthritis involving the wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, and proximal interphalangeal joints. He experienced fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and reported a 5-7 kg weight loss without fever or sweats. His pulmonary and joint symptoms were relieved by daily oral prednisone and flared with taper below 10 mg. Previous treatments included hydroxychloroquine 400 mg daily for 18 months and weekly adalimumab injections for 7 months, without improvement.

Numerous pink-purple dermal papules were present on the trunk and extremities, with preference for the extensor surfaces of the arms and legs. No lymphadenopathy was noted.

- Laboratory tests: Complete blood cell count, metabolic panel, hemoglobin A1c, viral and rheumatologic panels (including HIV), and serum/urine protein electrophoresis were normal or unremarkable.- Imaging studies:  - Chest radiograph: Normal  - High-resolution chest CT scan: Unremarkable  - Hand radiographs: Normal  - Echocardiography: Normal- Pulmonary Function Tests: Revealed mild restrictive disease with decreased forced vital capacity and total lung capacity- Pathology:  Image Title: Skin Biopsy Findings  Image Description: A) Pink-purple papules on extensor surface of arms  B) Nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate (H&E stain)  C) Admixed atypical, irregularly contoured lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes  D) Low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal (20x magnification)- Additional Testing:  - T-cell receptor PCR: Matching clonal rearrangements identified in 3 skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow sample  - Flow cytometry of bone marrow: Revealed lymphocytes with atypical CD3-negative, CD4-negative, CD5-positive, CD8-positive phenotype (2% of total cells)  - Immunostaining: Lymphocytes positive for CD3, inverted CD8:CD4 ratio, predominantly α/β positive

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified
B. Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, CD8+ variant
C. Mycosis fungoides (CD8-predominant variant)
D. CD8-positive granulomatous cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

excluded_candidates: Rheumatoid Arthritis: lack of response to hydroxychloroquine and adalimumab, and presence of atypical lymphocytes
Lupus: normal rheumatologic panels and absence of lymphadenopathy

static_evidence_items.content: Chief complaint: pink-purple dermal papules and polyarticular inflammatory arthritis
Symptoms: fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, 5-7 kg weight loss without fever or sweats
Relief of symptoms with daily oral prednisone, flare with taper below 10 mg
Previous treatments: hydroxychloroquine 400 mg daily for 18 months, weekly adalimumab injections for 7 months, without improvement
Numerous pink-purple dermal papules on trunk and extremities, preference for extensor surfaces of arms and legs
Laboratory tests: Complete blood cell count, metabolic panel, hemoglobin A1c, viral and rheumatologic panels, and serum/urine protein electrophoresis were normal or unremarkable
Imaging studies: Chest radiograph, High-resolution chest CT scan, Hand radiographs, and Echocardiography were normal or unremarkable
Pulmonary Function Tests: Revealed mild restrictive disease with decreased forced vital capacity and total lung capacity
Skin biopsy findings: Nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes, low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal
T-cell receptor PCR: Matching clonal rearrangements identified in 3 skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow sample
Flow cytometry of bone marrow: Revealed lymphocytes with atypical CD3-negative, CD4-negative, CD5-positive, CD8-positive phenotype
Immunostaining: Lymphocytes positive for CD3, inverted CD8:CD4 ratio, predominantly α/β positive
